newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Safeway to ring up stronger H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Safeway to ring up stronger H1.

text.p: Britain's fourth largest supermarket group, Safeway Plc, should give proof that its reorganisation has paid off with a rise in half-year profits and dividend when it reports on November 21, analysts said.
"These should be a strong set of results for Safeway, they should imply that management is in control and getting it right," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Safeway, which changed its name from Argyll earlier this year, should check in half-year pretax profits between 228 and 231 million stg, up from 213.7 million stg previously, and pay a dividend of 4.3 to 4.6 pence against 4.05 pence previously.
Its "Safeway 2000" strategic review, which aimed to cut costs and boost sales through refurbishment and reorganisation, was completed in the summer.

Safeway is now earning a reputation as an innovative retailer with moves such as self-scanning, where customers use an electronic device to track and add up their bill as they move round the store, avoiding time-wasting checkout queues.

The group's market share rose to around 10.4 percent in September according to industry figures, fourth behind market leader Tesco on 22.7 percent, J. Sainsbury at 19.3 percent and ASDA at 13.1 percent.

In the first half, analysts are looking for same-store sales to show a rise of around five percent over a year ago, a touch above figures from Sainsbury's but below Tesco's most recent 7.5 percent gain, reported in September.
"The trading environment (for supermarkets) is looking a bit more benign, consumer confidence is edging up and Safeway should have benefited," said the analyst.

A fierce petrol price war conducted earlier this year between supermarkets and oil companies is expected to have hit first-half profits, possibly by as much as 25 million stg at the operating level, analysts said.
But petrol prices are now picking up and with the key Christmas buying season ahead, Safeway is expected to boost performance in the second half.

"It could be a very good Christmas for supermarkets, they are gearing themselves better to the needs of shoppers and there is also some evidence of people buying more expensive brands," the analyst said.
Gross margins for Safeway are expected to be stable to slightly higher as prices in the sector see the pressure taken off by emphasis on loyalty cards and other customer benefits.
